name: Ganglioglioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of the Central Nervous System

criteria.description: Presence of both neoplastic mature ganglion cells and neoplastic glial cells on histopathological examination
MRI showing a well-demarcated, cystic and solid mass often with contrast enhancement in the temporal lobe or other CNS locations
Focal epilepsy or seizures refractory to medical treatment
Presence of BRAF V600E mutation in tumor tissue (optional supportive molecular finding)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of both neoplastic ganglion and glial components is required; supportive imaging and clinical features aid diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular testing for BRAF mutations can support diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Often drug-resistant and localized to tumor site
searchTerms: seizures starting in one area of brain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neurological deficits localized to tumor site

common.symptomName: Headache associated with increased intracranial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting due to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from increased brain pressure
vomiting due to raised intracranial pressure
headache with nausea caused by brain swelling
fluid buildup in brain from tumor blockage
brain swelling due to blocked fluid flow
water on the brain caused by tumor

rare.symptomName: Endocrine dysfunction due to hypothalamic involvement
searchTerms: hormone problems from brain area damage
endocrine issues due to hypothalamus involvement
hormonal imbalance caused by brain tumor

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
Histopathology showing mixed neuronal and glial tumor components
imaging: MRI with T1 hypointense and T2 hyperintense lesion with cystic and solid components
genetic: BRAF V600E mutation detected in approximately 20-60% of cases

distinguishingFeatures: Typically presents with seizures but histology lacks neoplastic ganglion cells
Predominantly glial tumor without neuronal components
Common in cerebellum and optic pathways, less often temporal lobe
Pure neuronal tumor without glial neoplastic component

redFlags: New onset of focal neurological deficits
Seizures refractory to multiple antiepileptic drugs
references: Louis DN, Perry A, Wesseling P, et al. WHO Classification of Tumours of the Central Nervous System, 5th Edition. IARC; 2021.

Koelsche C, Sahm F, Capper D, et al. BRAF V600E mutation is frequent in ganglioglioma and is associated with epileptogenicity. Acta Neuropathol. 2013;126(4): 617-619.
